$comment: Differences between the react-virtuoso 2 and 4 traces that are understood. Each names what differs and why; scenario, checkpoint and field are anchored regular expressions. Read by scripts/compare-virtuoso-traces.mts; an entry that matches nothing is reported as stale.

differences.reason: v4 hides a freshly mounted list until it reaches initialTopMostItemIndex: about 25 frames to the first visible item against v2's 1-2, where v2 shows the list at once and moves it into place over its first ~6 frames. Kept as is (decision for the upgrade), documented in ai-docs/ai-migration-v14-v15.md.

Scrolling up into messages not rendered yet, v2 jumps by the difference between their estimated and real heights (5-7 messages further per 400px here); v4 compensates and moves by the scrolled distance. The scroll invariant (content moves by exactly the scrolled distance) holds on v4 and fails on v2 in the fuzz runs.
v2 re-applies its initial scroll target for ~1.2s and undoes a scroll made meanwhile; v4 keeps the reader's scroll, so the next scroll reaches the top and loads an older page.

Both runtimes show the same messages at every step and keep the reader where they scrolled. On the first scroll after the jump the messages revealed at the top measure taller than v4 estimated, so for one pass its rendered range ends at m-0169 and the jumped-to message and the two after it (m-0170 to m-0172) leave it and remount; v4 renders messages more often around the jump for the same reason (more re-measuring passes). Every sampled frame of that scroll keeps the viewport covered on v4 (v2 shows one partly uncovered frame).
With a zero-height last item, v2 opens 8px short of the bottom; v4 opens at the bottom.

v4 marks GroupedVirtuoso group wrappers with data-index / data-item-index as it does items (v2 left them unmarked), so the first such element is now a month header. No SDK selector relies on it for grouped lists.

This scenario skips the mount measurement, so its one checkpoint spans the mount, where v4 commits a few more times while it positions the hidden list. Message renders fall (19 to 9) at the same time.

While it applies a prepend, v4 renders the items around the reader once more (before and after the same-paint scroll compensation): +7 message renders for the one older page this scenario loads, with the same final position and items. Across all scripted scenarios v4 renders fewer messages than v2.

v2 sometimes opens this 30-message channel at its top instead of its end (initialTopMostItemIndex `align: 'end'` loses a race with v2's initial scroll; it varies between runs); v4 opens it at the bottom, so every later step starts from a different place.

At the bottom of an older window: v2 reaches the bottom in this step and loads the next newer page at once; v4 ends this step 352px short (the revealed messages measure taller) and loads the same page in the next step. Same request, one step apart.

At the bottom of an older window, as in F-1001: v2 reports at-bottom in this step and loads the next newer page at once; on v4 the revealed messages re-measure (the list shrinks from 7072 to 6936px), it ends this step 204px short and loads nothing, and the next step jumps to the latest messages.

At the bottom of an older window, as in F-1001: the revealed messages re-measure and the list shrinks; v2 still reaches the bottom and loads the next newer page (then follows the new messages to the end), v4 ends this step 328px short (6536px list) and loads nothing.

Scrolling up to the top of the window: in some runs v2 stops about 175px short of the top (scrolling into messages not measured yet, as in B-20) and loads no older page; v4 reaches the top and loads it. Varies between runs, also without the focus-signal fix (1 in 3), so the entry is stale in runs where the two agree.
